title: Phase 9 · Stage 27: Lending over HTTP
summary: Turn every Result failure into a ProblemDetails response with the right status, catch crashes safely, and add the lending endpoints.

steps.title: One error shape, everywhere
body: Clients should be able to handle **every** error the same way. ASP.NET Core has a standard for that, **problem details** (RFC 9457): `application/problem+json` with `status`, `title` and `detail`. Three lines make the whole app use it:
app.UseExceptionHandler();              // an unhandled exception becomes a 500 problem, with no stack trace
app.UseStatusCodePages();               // a bare 404 or 400 gets a problem body too
The domain already says *why* something failed and *what kind* of failure it was: that is the `ErrorKind` you added in stage 10. One extension method maps it onto HTTP for every endpoint:
public static IResult ToProblem<T>(this Result<T> result) => Results.Problem(

steps.prompt: Match each failure to the status `ToProblem` gives it.
steps.explain: NotFound and Conflict come from the domain; anything thrown is a bug and becomes a 500 that reveals nothing.
The same switch shape as `ToProblem`: two specific arms and a catch-all.

steps.prompt: Why does `UseExceptionHandler` answer with a generic 500 problem instead of the exception message?
options: Messages and stack traces can leak internals to attackers; clients only need to know the server failed
steps.explain: Log the details on the server, return nothing sensitive to the client. The tests check that *Boom* never appears in the body.

steps.title: ProblemDetails and POST /loans
prompt: 1. Register `AddProblemDetails()`; after seeding, add `app.UseExceptionHandler();` and `app.UseStatusCodePages();`. Add `app.MapGet("/debug/crash", IResult () => throw new InvalidOperationException("Boom"));` to prove a crash is a 500 problem that does not mention *Boom*.
2. Add `ResultHttp.ToProblem` from the card, and use it for the 409s in `POST /books` and `POST /members`.

3. Add `record LoanDto(int Id, string Isbn, int MemberId, DateOnly LoanedOn, DateOnly DueOn, DateOnly? ReturnedOn, bool Renewed)` with `From(Loan)`, and `record CreateLoanRequest(string? Isbn, int? MemberId)`.

4. `POST /loans` `{"isbn":"978-0441172719","memberId":2}`: missing isbn or memberId → 400 `ValidationProblem` with key `loan` (`Both isbn and memberId are required.`); otherwise `library.Lend`: **201** `Location: /loans/{id}` with the `LoanDto`, or `ToProblem()`.
5. `GET /loans` lists every loan; `GET /loans?active=true` only active ones, `false` only returned ones.

// "a,b,c" from one property of every item in a JSON array, so one row checks which items came back, in order.
static string Keys(JsonElement json, string property) => json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array
? string.Join(",", json.EnumerateArray().Select(e => DojoWeb.Prop(e, property)))
: "(not a JSON array: " + json.ValueKind + ")";
static JsonElement At(JsonElement json, int index) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && index < json.GetArrayLength() ? json[index] : default;
static JsonElement Get(JsonElement json, string property) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object && json.TryGetProperty(property, out var value) ? value : default;
static async Task<JsonElement> GetJson(HttpClient http, string url) => await DojoWeb.Json(await http.GetAsync(url));
static bool IsProblem(HttpResponseMessage r) => r.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType == "application/problem+json";
static string? First(JsonElement errors, string key) { var list = Get(errors, key); return list.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array && list.GetArrayLength() > 0 ? list[0].GetString() : null; }
